briefings.title: BREAKING: Trump Signs Executive Order On Psychedelic Drugs With Joe Rogan As Iran Shuts Hormuz
briefings.tldr: President Trump signed a landmark executive order to fast-track the research, clinical approval, and rescheduling of psychedelic therapies—specifically Ibogaine—to combat the national opioid crisis and the veteran suicide epidemic.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump signed a landmark executive order to fast-track the research, clinical approval, and rescheduling of psychedelic therapies—specifically Ibogaine—to combat the national opioid crisis and the veteran suicide epidemic. The move marks a significant shift from the "daily pill" model of mental health to one-time treatments designed to address treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, and addiction.

## The Origins and Motivation of the Order
* **Joe Rogan’s Role:** The initiative began with a direct communication from podcaster Joe Rogan to President Trump regarding the efficacy of Ibogaine. 
    * **Addiction Stats:** Rogan noted that with 80,000 annual overdose deaths and 5 million opiate addicts, Ibogaine shows an 80-90% success rate in ending addiction with just one or two doses.
    * **Policy Shift:** The order aims to reverse the "harmful" restrictions of the 1970 Controlled Substances Act, which speakers argued was passed for political rather than medical reasons.
* **The Veteran Crisis:** President Trump emphasized that the veteran suicide rate is a "national tragedy," noting that since 9/11, 21 times more veterans have been lost to suicide than to battlefield combat.
* **The "Right to Try" Expansion:** The order utilizes the "Right to Try" law to grant terminally or desperately ill patients immediate access to these breakthrough therapies while they undergo the standard FDA approval process.

## Clinical Efficacy and Veteran Testimonials
* **Failure of Traditional Antidepressants:** Speakers, including HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Dr. Marty Makary, noted that standard antidepressants have only a 20-30% remission rate and often require lifetime usage.
* **Success Stories:**
    * **Marcus Luttrell (Ret. Navy SEAL):** Reported that Ibogaine "absolutely changed my life for the better" five years ago, moving him from a "victim" mindset to reclaiming his life.
    * **Rob O'Neill (Ret. Navy SEAL):** Stated the treatment fixed a "demonic relationship with alcohol" and saved his life and his marriage.
    * **Morgan Luttrell (US Representative):** Noted the treatment allowed him to get off opiates and sleep for the first time in a decade.
* **Paradigm Shift:** The administration is moving toward "precision mental health," focusing on one-time treatments that create new neural pathways rather than chronic symptom management.

## Federal Implementation and Fast-Tracking
* **FDA "National Priority Vouchers":** Commissioner Marty Makary announced that the FDA will issue three vouchers to expedite psychedelic drug reviews.
    * **Accelerated Timeline:** Under this program, drug approvals could take weeks rather than a year or more.
    * **Human Trials:** The FDA has issued the first-ever Ibogaine investigational new drug clearance for human trials in the U.S.
* **Funding and Research:**
    * **Federal Investment:** The federal government is committing $50 million to Ibogaine research, matching a $50 million commitment from the state of Texas.
    * **Scientific Rigor:** Dr. Jay Bhattacharya (NIH) and Dr. Nora Volkow (NIDA) will oversee "gold standard" science to understand *how* these drugs work and ensure safe administration protocols.
* **Rescheduling:** The order directs the DEA and DOJ to begin the rescheduling process for any psychedelic drug that achieves FDA approval.

## Cost, Access, and the "MAHA" Initiative
* **Pricing and Insurance:** Dr. Mehmet Oz (CMS) is tasked with creating models (CMMI) to ensure these treatments are affordable and accessible through Medicare, Medicaid, and the VA.
* **Drug Cost Reform:** Trump highlighted the "Most Favored Nations" pricing strategy, claiming it will reduce drug costs by 50-80% by ensuring the U.S. pays the lowest price available globally.
* **The MAHA Connection:** Secretary RFK Jr. linked the order to the "Make America Healthy Again" (MAHA) movement, targeting the underlying causes of the U.S. mental health crisis, which he claims is the most expensive health issue in the country.

> "With one dose of Ibogaine, more than 80% of people are free of that addiction. With two doses, it's more than 90%. . . . These drugs are illegal not because they're harmful, they're illegal because of the 1970 Controlled Substances Act. . . We're free of that now." — **Joe Rogan**

> "We lose 21 times more [veterans to suicide than on the battlefield]. And today we’re bringing them new hope. I think you’re going to see a big difference and a big reduction in that number." — **President Donald Trump**

> "This is an entire paradigm shift away from a one-a-day pill model which has failed so many. And for the many who are treatment-resistant . . . this offers them a way of getting out of that rut." — **Dr. Marty Makary**

> "I went through a lot of the programs that the veterans are going through and I always kind of felt like I was a victim. . . When I came out of [Ibogaine treatment], I felt like I had gotten my life back." — **Marcus Luttrell**

briefings.title: Class Disrupted Live: Reed Hastings on the AI-Powered Future of Learning | ASU+GSV Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Reed Hastings reflects on decades of education reform and EdTech before arguing that AI-powered individualized tutoring will finally replace the traditional "sage on a stage" classroom model, potentially doubling learning rates by shifting teachers into social-emotional roles.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Reed Hastings reflects on decades of education reform and EdTech before arguing that AI-powered individualized tutoring will finally replace the traditional "sage on a stage" classroom model, potentially doubling learning rates by shifting teachers into social-emotional roles.

## Historical Reflections on Education Reform
* **State Policy and District Leadership:**
  * **The Hero Syndrome:** Reform efforts under No Child Left Behind and leaders like Roy Romer (LAUSD, seven-year record tenure) raised scores temporarily.
  * **Systemic Dismantling:** Succeeding administrations routinely dismantled these programs within five to ten years regardless of results, leading Reed Hastings to conclude there is "very little to show for it."
* **Charter School Progress:**
  * **Trench Warfare:** Charter networks have not failed, but growth is "grindingly slow," fighting to a draw in blue states while expanding in red states (Florida, Texas, Arizona, Georgia).
  * **City-Level Impact:** High charter share is the only strategy driving city-wide gap closure for poor students, ranging from modest gains at 10% share to massive gap closure in 100% charter New Orleans over 25 years.
* **Early EdTech Realities:**
  * **DreamBox Learning:** An early adaptive learning pioneer hindered by the friction of selling to school districts and charters.
  * **The Grammar of Schooling:** Districts valued adaptive software only for catching kids up to grade level, explicitly asking to disable features that let students get ahead because advanced students disrupted the classroom.

## The Exponential Trajectory of AI
* **The Doubling Curve:** AI quality is currently doubling every year, compressing timelines for societal breakthroughs in cancer treatment, free energy, and autonomy.
* **Societal Trade-Offs and Perspective:**
  * **Car Accident Comparison:** The U.S. loses 40,000 lives annually to car accidents (500,000 globally), a societal trade-off we implicitly accept.
  * **AI Risk vs. Reward:** While tragic individual AI- or self-driving-related deaths draw intense focus, society risks losing perspective on the massive scale of human life AI and autonomous systems will ultimately save.

## The Future of Learning: Beyond the "Sage on the Stage"
* **The Steam Factory Analogy:** 
  * 1800s factories relied on a single central steam engine powering a complex web of belts, pulleys, and rods. 
  * Economists were baffled when early electric factories merely swapped the steam engine for a big electric motor without major productivity gains.
  * True productivity exploded only when factories adopted individualized electric motors for every loom.
  * **Education Parallel:** The classroom's "sage on a stage" is the old power distribution system holding back technology; true transformation requires removing it entirely in favor of individualized, mastery-based daily lesson plans.
* **Redefining the Teacher's Role:**
  * **Social-Emotional Specialists:** Teachers pivot from direct instruction to emotional maturity, circle work, and social development.
  * **Holistic Peer Interaction:** Just as competitive 10-year-old chess players tutored by AI still play chess together, students retain collaborative projects and socialization while academic instruction is individualized.

## Global Scale and International Equity
* **Shareable Technology:** While exporting physical charter models like KIPP or Success Academy to international contexts is exceptionally difficult, software and AI teaching models are instantly shareable.
* **Rwanda Test Lab:** Partnering with CJ and Ben Rosen (RESSGG) on a "one tablet per child" initiative in Rwanda, creating a sandbox for U.S. application developers to test models aimed at making Rwanda a top educational system globally.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Reed Hastings** predicts that comprehensive, one-on-one AI tutoring will prove that students can learn at twice the speed of traditional schooling—meaning an 8th grader will possess the knowledge of a typical high schooler, and an 11th grader will match a typical college student.
* **Reed Hastings** predicts that future EdTech entrepreneurs who build pure-play, self-teaching, individualized systems rather than selling workflow tools to traditional districts will successfully skate to where the puck is going.

## Notable Quotes
> "Whatever challenge you think AI is not up to, just wait a year."
> — Reed Hastings

> "We have to be brave enough to try to do school without sage on a stage at all... to have all of school be learning individually, your daily lesson plan from the system, executing."
> — Reed Hastings

> "If you want to make money selling to a school district, make teachers' lives easier. If you want to change the world, focus on the homeschoolers... and build systems that are individualized."
> — Reed Hastings

briefings.title: Myntra Founder: Will AI Replace Software Engineers? The Truth
briefings.tldr: The gap between imagination and product execution has collapsed, allowing a single individual with AI to perform the work of entire departments in days.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The gap between imagination and product execution has collapsed, allowing a single individual with AI to perform the work of entire departments in days. Future success belongs to those who shift from being managers of people to "AI managers" who leverage curiosity and agency to command near-infinite technical resources.

## The Collapse of Traditional Software Engineering
* **Rapid Prototyping:** Mukesh Bansal notes that projects which previously cost $100,000 and months of development can now be built for roughly $5,000 in credits and 10 days of work.
    * Development cycles have shifted from months/quarters to days/weeks; building a functional V1 in a single day is becoming a realistic expectation.
* **AI-Generated Codebases:** Approximately 90% of modern software code is now AI-generated.
    * Developers are moving from writing code to "vibe coding," where the primary tasks are specification, code review, and testing rather than manual syntax entry.
* **The "Enrico" Model:** Peeyush Ranjan highlights his AI "Chief of Staff," Enrico, as the most productive employee at his company, Fermi AI.
    * Enrico has global memory of the company, can interview its creator to write its own PRDs, and implements new capabilities autonomously within minutes.

## The Rise of the "AI Manager" and the New Org Chart
* **Revenue Per Employee:** Traditional Indian IT services (like TCS) generate ~$40k–$50k per employee, while AI-native vertical companies are aiming for $3M–$5M per employee.
* **Problem-Solving Loops:** Companies are moving away from hierarchical management structures in favor of "problem-solving loops" where AI agents handle information flow and task execution.
* **Management Reinvention:**
    * **Manager to IC:** In the AI era, senior leaders (including CTOs and CEOs) are returning to being "hands-on" builders. 
    * **Resource Management:** Being a manager now means managing "infinite resources" (AI) rather than motivating human teams. This requires asking better questions and providing structured specifications.
* **Wipeout of Traditional Knowledge Work:** Product managers, middle managers, and engineers who do not reinvent themselves as AI-fluent builders are at high risk of being "wiped out" within months or quarters.

## The New Talent Moat: Curiosity and Agency
* **The Obsolescence of "Non-Technical":** The label "non-technical" is disappearing. AI has lowered the bar so much that anyone with a vision can instantiate software.
* **Premium Skills:** When intelligence becomes a commodity utility, the following traits become the new competitive advantage:
    * **Agency:** The drive to act without waiting for permission or direction.
    * **Curiosity:** The willingness to dig deep into how to utilize AI horsepower.
    * **System-Level Thinking:** The ability to understand building blocks, second-order effects, and architectural scaling.
    * **Lived Experience:** Nuanced knowledge that isn't easily aggregated by a model.
* **Cognitive Debt:** A significant risk is "atrophying" cognitive capabilities—becoming intellectually lazy and over-reliant on AI output without critical verification.

## Distribution as the Ultimate Bottleneck
* **Innovation as a Commodity:** Because startups can now innovate at the same speed as large companies, "innovation" is no longer a sustainable moat.
* **The Distribution Moat:** Distribution (customer access, trust, and brand) has become the most precious asset.
    * **Startup Challenge:** If a startup lacks distribution, an incumbent can simply clone their AI-driven innovation and ship it to an existing user base immediately.
* **Personalization vs. Monopolies:**
    * AI allows for a "Product-Market Fit of One" through extreme personalization.
    * This could lead to a "Law Firm" model of business: small, high-revenue teams (e.g., 10 people) controlling a billion-dollar niche because their AI is so deeply personalized to their specific clients that switching costs are too high.

## Notable Quotes

> "The gap between imagination and instantiation has shrunk so much that every day when I think of something... it’s like ten minutes later." — **Peeyush Ranjan**

> "If you have a compelling idea, just build the whole damn product in a week. It wouldn't be surprised when it is in a day." — **Mukesh Bansal**

> "Everybody's gonna be AI managers. All our jobs will be how do you manage this resource given to you." — **Peeyush Ranjan**

> "Most people who are in the knowledge work business... if they are today not calling timeout on whatever they are doing and absolutely committing to reinvent themselves, they are going to get completely wiped out." — **Mukesh Bansal**

briefings.title: Sam Altman’s Attack, Amazon vs. Starlink, and What Opus 4.7 Actually Means | #248
briefings.tldr: Anthropic's Opus 4.7 dropped to mixed reviews amid rising AI anxiety and physical backlash, while the Stanford 2026 AI Index highlighted soaring benchmarks alongside youth hiring freezes and falling model transparency.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Anthropic's Opus 4.7 dropped to mixed reviews amid rising AI anxiety and physical backlash, while the Stanford 2026 AI Index highlighted soaring benchmarks alongside youth hiring freezes and falling model transparency.

## Anthropic Opus 4.7 & Technical Shifts
* **Model Release Reception:** Released just hours before recording, Anthropic's Opus 4.7 was described by Alex Wiesner-Gross as "moderately interesting" rather than mythically interesting or incrementally new, feeling like an expectation-anchoring point release or distillation of an existing model. Dave noted it dropped easily into Cursor and Claude Co-worker, smoothly installed its own updates via computer use, and returned elaborate budget estimates.
* **Deprecation of Hyperparameters:** **Removal of Dials:** Hyperparameters like the temperature knob and explicit reasoning-token counts have been removed. Natural language prompts are now the primary guidance tool for determinism and agent behavior (e.g., specifying sub-agent counts in text).
* **Multimodal and Architectural Focus:** 
  * **Image Processing:** Image input sizes are **3x bigger**, significantly improving corporate diagram, PowerPoint, and PDF scanning.
  * **Missing Output Generation:** Opus still cannot generate images (producing "absolute garbage" diagrams), which Wiesner-Gross attributes to Anthropic focusing ruthlessly on economic value per token rather than text-vs-image productivity.

## Stanford 2026 AI Index & Labor Market Shifting
* **Stanford 2026 AI Index Findings:** Highlighted by host Peter Diamandis, the 9th annual report notes SWE benchmark scores rising from **60% to 97%**, global Gen AI adoption hitting **53%** in three years, China leading research publications (**30 notable models** vs US **50**), and model transparency scores dropping from **58 to 40**. Public optimism sits at just **23%**, contrasted with **73%** among experts.
* **Youth Employment Impact:** **Early-Career Hiring Freeze:** Software developer employment for ages **22–25** dropped **nearly 20% since 2024**, while older developer headcount grew. Rather than mass layoffs, companies are simply not hiring junior workers, prompting calls for young professionals to leverage their skills into entrepreneurship immediately before ASI commoditizes them.
* **Geographic Density:** Panellists emphasized the high density of technical founders in the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston as critical for risk-taking and rapid recovery from startup failures.

## AI Backlash, Security, and Data Center Friction
* **Physical Unrest:** A **20-year-old Texan** linked to the PauseAI Discord threw a Molotov cocktail at Sam Altman's San Francisco home, carrying a manifesto with executive addresses and a kill list, followed three days later by gunshots at Altman's Russian Hill property.
* **Data Center Pushback:** **Regulatory Resistance:** Citizens in Festus, Missouri ousted half their city council after they approved a **$6 billion data center on 360 acres**, while Maine passed the US's first statewide data center ban (**18-month moratorium**). Between March and June, **$98 billion** in data centers was blocked or delayed across **11 states**. Panellists dismissed water-usage concerns as political theater.
* **Workforce Replacement:** Skilled workers over **50** and former professionals (such as a **$500k/year** emergency MD) are turning to AI data annotation ($20–$40/hr) as bridge jobs, while automated systems like Tesla/xAI's "MacroHard" observe employee keyboard/mouse interactions to simulate and replace traditional corporate workflows.

## Infrastructure, Algorithmic Breakthroughs, and Autonomous Business
* **Amazon vs. Starlink:** Amazon acquired Globalstar for **$11.57 billion** (holding **25 satellites** and **25.225 megahertz** of globally authorized ITU spectrum across **120 countries**) and partnered with Apple to provide satellite capabilities, setting up a direct challenge to SpaceX's Starlink network (which operates **10,000 satellites** and prepares V3 Starship launches delivering **1 terabit/sec** downlink capacity per satellite).
* **Google TurboQuant:** Google published a quantization breakthrough reducing memory usage by **6x** and boosting attention computation performance by **8x**, driving KV cache down to **1 bit** and enabling larger context windows. Developers reverse-engineered it within a week.
* **Autonomous Retail:** Andon Labs opened a fully AI-controlled store in San Francisco's Cow Hollow neighbourhood where an AI bot named "Luna" posted a job on Indeed, conducted Zoom interviews, hired a human employee (Felix), and selected inventory.

## Transhumanism, Enhanced Sports, and Speciation
* **The Enhanced Games:** Founded by Christian Angermayer, Peter Thiel, and Aron D'Souza, the Enhanced Games allow medical and pharmacological enhancements in swimming, track, and weightlifting, offering **$25 million** in prize money on the Las Vegas Strip for Memorial Day weekend **2026**, backed by a planned SPAC reverse merger.
* **Humanity's Evolutionary Forks:** Diamandis proposed five major evolutionary forks for human speciation: creator vs. consumer, longevity escape velocity, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), Earth vs. stars (space settlement), and digital uploads (destructive vs. non-destructive consciousness transfer). Panellists debated the viability of immortality, cybernetic integration, and interstellar colonization.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "Apple in short turn ends up pitting Amazon, the new Globalstar owner, against SpaceX's Starlink to have at least two vendors for global space to cell phone service and this becomes the new alternative to terrestrial networks in two to three years." — Alex Wiesner-Gross
* "This is going to be a 100x year... it's going to be 100x by summer." — Dave (referencing AI performance scaling)
* "The max depth right now is probably five folks between me and anyone in the company. I would want to get that down to two to three this year. And in the most ideal case, there is no layer, everyone in the company reports to me. And that would be all 6,000 of the company." — Jack Dorsey

## Notable Quotes
> "The irony of the PauseAI so-called movement is that it has done nothing except accelerate AI capabilities."
> — Alex Wiesner-Gross

> "All capitalism is worker arbitrage. You hire somebody for 20 bucks an hour and they make you 100 bucks an hour. Your challenge what you're talking about is how do you equitably share that outcome."
> — Salim Ismail

> "You're dealing with a legacy institution here... getting Stanford to move is like pushing a glacier."
> — Peter Diamandis
